title: CELEUS: Certifiable and Efficient LLM Evaluation via E-Processes
claim: Our method reaches the target precision with far fewer evaluated samples than the baseline, approaching the oracle bound.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, shared legend on top, dashed target line with markers
description: Three line-plot panels in a row, one each for SST-2, MMLU and AG News, sharing a legend across the top. The x-axis is evaluated samples and the y-axis is confidence interval width. Each panel has four curves with shaded standard-deviation bands: a solid red CELEUS curve, a dashed pale-red CELEUS without surrogate curve, a teal Oracle curve and a dark slate-gray baseline e-value curve. All curves decay with more samples. The baseline stays well above the others, while CELEUS sits close to the Oracle. A horizontal dashed gray line marks epsilon = 0.05. A teal star and a red triangle mark the median number of labels needed to reach epsilon. The red triangle sits just right of the star, and both are far left of where the baseline would reach it. The eye goes first to the gap between the slate baseline and the red and teal curves.
caption: CI width versus the number of evaluated samples. Each trajectory averages the mean widths of the six surrogate--target pairs, with each pair averaged over $50$ seeds. Shaded bands show $\pm 1$ standard deviation across these pair means. The dashed line marks $\epsilon=0.05$.
abstract: Can we trust evaluation scores to capture an LLM's true real-world performance? Certifiable evaluation answers this question by providing a confidence interval (CI) that covers the LLM's true performance with high probability (e.g., 95%). In particular, existing methods sequentially select evaluation samples from a fixed pool and keep updating the CI until certain conditions are satisfied, e.g., the CI width reaches a target precision. However, existing methods are not generally anytime-valid: the claimed coverage (e.g., 95%) may fail when CIs are repeatedly updated and used to decide when to stop, leaving a gap between theoretical rigor and practice. This paper bridges this gap by proposing CELEUS, a Certifiable framework for Efficient LLM evaluation, which leverages E-processes to build anytime-valid CIs. Concretely, we propose a new signal that combines two ingredients: (i) Uncertainty-guided sampling to select informative samples for evaluation, and (ii) Surrogate-assisted approximations for unevaluated samples. We prove that the new signal remains unbiased for the evaluation score conditional on the past, enabling statistically-grounded and anytime-valid e-process CIs. More importantly, the two ingredients reduce estimation variance and help reach the target precision with fewer evaluated samples. We also prove that CIs obtained by CELEUS can shrink at a near-parametric rate up to logarithmic factors and analyze the oracle variance-optimal sampling rule that motivates the empirical uncertainty-guided one. Experiments show that CELEUS reaches the target precision using 54-62% fewer evaluated samples than baselines, while preserving anytime-valid coverage. Code is available at https://github.com/zyecs/celeus.
